entries.brief: ONE improved eighteenth-century HORSE-DRAWN WOOD-AND-IRON SINGLE-SHARE SWING PLOUGH, inspired by the early Rotherham family. The long stout oak draw beam runs diagonally forward, clearly connected to a compact solid working body near its rear; two raised wooden steering handles rise behind the working body. A sharp dark iron vertical coulter hangs from the beam immediately IN FRONT of the triangular horizontal ploughshare; directly behind that share a coherent curved iron-faced MOULDBOARD turns outward to lift a furrow. Clearly show the three distinct connected cutting parts, not a random pile of iron. Weathered brown oak, neutral charcoal iron with restrained worn edge highlights. Entire beam, two handles, share and curved mouldboard visible. Angle the apparatus into a compact diagonal composition, without shortening it into an implausible miniature. No wheels, seed hopper, row of tines, harrow, separate fork, sack, seeds, soil clump, horse, person or field. No modern detachable-share fittings or steel slade of post-1800 museum modifications. This is a simplified eighteenth-century concept, not an exact museum replica or universally applicable national model.

entries.brief: ONE traditional HAND PAPERMAKING APPARATUS consisting of a broad low oval oak-stave VAT with two dark iron hoops, filled nearly to the rim with pale ivory watery RAG-PULP SLURRY, and ONE large RECTANGULAR WOOD-FRAMED WIRE PAPER MOULD with its fitted removable wooden DECKLE rim. The vat and mould are one coherent process group. The rectangular mould is inclined gently above the vat, its lower short edge resting on a clearly visible wooden support bar spanning the rim, its higher edge leaning against the far rim; no floating tray or invisible support. Show the face of the fine closely laid wire screen: a thin near-white wet fiber layer covers most of it while a small edge area reveals neutral brown-gray wire mesh. A few small clear water drips fall from the low mould edge INTO the vat, never outside onto imaginary ground. Clearly readable cream liquid inside a wooden vessel and a large rectangular sheet-forming frame distinguish this from a cooking pot or washing basket. Natural warm wood, dull iron, off-white pulp; no copper-focused subject or bright colored chemical. No finished paper stack, envelopes, letters, loose blank sheets, screw press, additional moulds, ladle, furniture, person or scenery. Inspired by preindustrial European hand papermaking documented in the Encyclopedie of 1767, a simplified isolated technology apparatus, not an entire paper mill.

entries.brief: Same organized hand-tool workbench, but wheel disassembled flat on its tabletop: partially attached hub/spokes and rim arc, plus clearly separated spokes and rim pieces. Empty vise; no wood interpenetration.
entries.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: ONE transparent TECHNOLOGY icon for Victoria 3, Ateliers organisés.
Input image 1: EDIT TARGET — the existing painted wooden workbench with organized tool rack and an upright cart wheel apparently intersecting the tabletop.
Primary request: Change ONLY the wheel/workpiece and its immediate contact area to show a wooden wheel DISASSEMBLED DURING REPAIR. REMOVE the entire upright assembled wheel, including every part apparently going through the bench. Restore an intact continuous tabletop where it stood. Leave the front vise empty, clearly separate from the wheel parts.
Repair arrangement: lay a PARTIALLY DISMANTLED WOODEN WHEEL FLAT ON THE LEFT HALF OF THE BENCH TOP, viewed obliquely from above. The central round hub lies with its axle hole facing upward. THREE spokes are still coherently attached to that hub, forming a fan and reaching ONE curved rim arc that covers roughly half the circumference; the opposite half is open and visibly incomplete. Nearby, THREE detached tapered wooden spokes and TWO separate curved wooden rim segments lie neatly on the same tabletop, with clear spaces between pieces and readable mortise/tenon connections. All of these pieces belong to ONE wheel under repair, not several miniature wheels. Make the thick pale oak hub and curved rim pieces large and readable at icon size.
Physical constraints: every wheel component rests wholly ABOVE the tabletop on a visible support/contact surface. No piece passes through the table, hangs unsupported, pokes through the front apron, fuses into tools, crosses a leg, or floats in midair. Show coherent depth and short natural contact shadows on the tabletop. No complete upright wheel remains anywhere. No broken jagged shards, iron tyre, exploded-view arrows or dramatic destruction; this is orderly artisan repair.
Invariants: keep the bench's overall shape, camera angle, legs, lower shelf, upright connected tool-rack backboard, arranged manual tools, warm oak and neutral dark iron colors, fine matte painted texture and soft upper-left light. Keep existing hand tools, but shift the few tabletop tools slightly to the right ONLY if needed to leave clear repair space. Do not redesign the cabinet or bench, add tools, people, modern machinery, extra furniture, floor, room, wall, frame, text, watermark or scenery.
Output: ONE square high-resolution icon, at least 1024 pixels, with the complete workstation inside generous transparent margins. Preserve genuine transparent alpha outside and through the bench gaps. No black/white/checkerboard fake backdrop, uniform blue/sepia cast or external ground shadow. Only this wheel-repair correction; the other two technology icons are not input or edit targets.
